title: Deploy Readiness, Capacity & Cost Roadmap Handoff
summary: Quarterly health/check-in focused on upcoming deploy readiness for BlueHarbor's customer-facing features. Main themes: recent cost spike on embedding workloads, capacity planning for holiday traffic, decision between staying hosted vs moving critical routes to Dedicated (or VPC), security/audit evidence requests, and an agreed pilot and benchmarking plan. AE/SE to hand off to Customer Success for pilot execution and to share detailed cost export and security pack.
topics: Recent 30% token cost spike on nightly batch jobs
Capacity surge plan for Black Friday-like traffic
Dedicated vs Hosted routing for high-SLA endpoints
VPC/private deployment constraints and audit logs
Pilot: 2-week dedicated route benchmark and cost comparison
action_items: Layla Brooks: Provide list of top 10 endpoints and expected p95 latency SLA (due: 2026-07-20)
Sofia Alvarez: Share 30-day token-level cost export and the cost-breakdown spreadsheet (due: 2026-07-15)
Marcus Liu: Run a baseline perf test (hosted) for the top 3 endpoints and deliver logs (due: 2026-07-22)
BlueHarbor/SRE (Jordan): Provide example infra diagram and VPC peering constraints (due: 2026-07-19)
Keisha Nair: Confirm business timeline for feature launch and must-have SLAs (due: 2026-07-18)
next_steps: Redwood to propose Dedicated pilot configuration with autoscale knobs and expected cost ranges
Customer to decide whether to run pilot in Hosted with special routing or in Dedicated capacity
Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive (SE-led) next week to finalize benchmarking metrics
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Alvarez: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Is this a good time?
[00:03] Amit Desai: Yeah, good here. We gotta squeeze this in before the exec sync so appreciate it.
[00:08] Layla Brooks: Morning, all — afternoon for some of us. Want to focus on readiness and the cost spike we saw last month.
[00:15] Sofia Alvarez: Totally. Marcus and I will walk through what we saw from our side and then we want to hand off a clear pilot and next steps to the CS team.
[00:22] Marcus Liu: Quick intro — I'm Marcus, SE on the account. I'll cover perf numbers and batching/kv cache suggestions.
[00:28] Jordan Park: Jordan, SRE. We'll talk capacity, and I have questions about VPC peering.
[00:32] Keisha Nair: Keisha, PM — timeline side, we have a soft launch window in late Sep. Need clarity on SLA.
[00:37] [00:45] Sofia Alvarez: Ok, so first item — cost. We noticed your embedding pipeline ran a reindexing job around 2026-06-23 that increased token volume by ~30% over baseline for 72 hours. Layla, do you recall any config change?
[00:53] Layla Brooks: Yeah that was a manual rerun, we bumped batch size to 512 to speed it up but apparently we didn't account for prefix reuse, so lots of duplicated tokens. My bad.
[01:02] Marcus Liu: That makes sense. Larger batches in a reindex often amplify token counts if prefix caching isn't used. We can recommend a different batching profile and KV cache keying to avoid re-sending identical prefixes.
[01:12] Jordan Park: Is that something we can fix on our side quickly or do we need you to tweak anything?
[01:15] Marcus Liu: Mostly on your side — change the client to keep consistent prefix ids — but we can provide a snippet in the SDK. Also there are quantization options that reduce per-token compute for embeddings.
[01:23] Amit Desai: Quick Q — if we move those heavy jobs to Dedicated, do we buy down unit cost? What are the tradeoffs on latency vs cost?
[01:29] Sofia Alvarez: Good question. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and sometimes a lower effective per-token cost for heavy recurring batch jobs, but it adds a commit/contract and you'd lose on-demand scale in other regions. We usually recommend Dedicated for steady-state high-volume background pipelines and keep low-latency customer-facing routes on Hosted or VPC.
[01:38] [01:45] Keisha Nair: For the customer-facing routes, latency p95 needs to be under 180ms. Can you hit that on Hosted?
[01:49] Marcus Liu: Depends on model and sequence length. For typical chat/generation at 256 tokens we see p95 ~120-160ms in our hosted default in us-west, but tail varies. If you need 120ms consistently, Dedicated with pinned model instances and optimized kernels is safer.
[02:04] Layla Brooks: Security — our auditors want proof of encryption at rest and KMS integration for the keys used on the private deployment. Can Redwood provide SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration docs?
[02:13] Sofia Alvarez: Yes — we have a security pack with SOC 2 Type II summary, SSO/SAML flows, and KMS/HSM patterns for private deployments. We'll share the pack after this call.
[02:21] Jordan Park: Also need to know if audit logs include token-level routing decisions — like which requests hit Dedicated vs fallback.
[02:25] Marcus Liu: Auditing captures per-request route, model version, and latency metrics. The logs won't contain prompt text unless you enable that retention, we can show you the schema.
[02:32] [02:45] Keisha Nair: Back to cost — the spike was troubling; can you run a token-level cost projection for the next quarter if we do a mix of Dedicated for batch and Hosted for front-end?
[02:53] Sofia Alvarez: Yep. I'll drop the 30-day export and a modeled projection for a split configuration. Expect a spreadsheet with scenarios: 100% Hosted, Hosted + Dedicated for batch, and Dedicated for everything.
[03:02] Amit Desai: For Dedicated what commit sizes do you recommend? We don't want to overcommit.
[03:07] Marcus Liu: We can propose conservative commits with burst capacity enabled. For example, if your nightly embedding job is X tokens/day, commit to ~1.5x steady state and use burst for peak processing windows. We'll show cost delta.
[03:19] [03:30] Jordan Park: Regarding VPC — we can't do outbound peering to third-party infra except through an approved egress pattern. Will Redwood Private fit into our current network model?
[03:36] Sofia Alvarez: Our Private control plane can sit in your VPC with peered endpoints, or we can do an on-prem package. There are common patterns: VPC endpoint + mTLS and customer KMS. Marcus, want to add nuance?
[03:45] Marcus Liu: Sure — for low-latency private calls we recommend colocated inference in your region and we support route-level pinning. There are firewall rules and route table changes that teams typically need to approve. The SRE will need to share current egress/ingress constraints.
[03:59] [04:10] Keisha Nair: Timeline check — if we decide Dedicated pilot, how long until we can run a pilot benchmark?
[04:14] Sofia Alvarez: Typical pilot setup is 2-3 weeks from contract signature for Dedicated pool provisioning; hosted-only benchmarking can start within a few days.
[04:21] Layla Brooks: We want the pilot by early August ideally. Is that feasible?
[04:25] Marcus Liu: If we do hosted benchmarking, yes within a week. Dedicated pilot by early Aug is tight but possible if commit approval moves quickly.
[04:31] [04:40] Amit Desai: Ok let's talk metrics — what should we measure in the pilot?
[04:44] Marcus Liu: Good metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, variance under load, error rate, and real-workload end-to-end latency from client to response. Also KV cache hit ratio for repeated prefixes.
[04:56] Jordan Park: We'll want tracing hooks and a simple test harness we can run in our CI.
[05:00] Marcus Liu: We'll provide a load harness and a reproducible test plan. We'll also include guidelines to reproduce the 30% spike scenario safely.
[05:07] [05:25] Keisha Nair: Who's the single point person for the pilot?
[05:28] Sofia Alvarez: For Redwood it'll be Marcus for technical and me for commercial. For BlueHarbor, Layla will own the coordination. We'll get a joint kickoff doc.
[05:36] Layla Brooks: Sounds good. Also, small ask — can you recommend quantization settings to reduce GPU usage without regressing embedding quality? We care about recall.
[05:42] Marcus Liu: Yes, we have recommended quantization profiles per model class. For embeddings we recommend 8-bit quantization with per-channel scaling for production; we can run a quality regression test on your sample dataset.
[05:51] [06:00] Amit Desai: Any known competitor nuances — like if we switch to Anthropic model routes, would that change costs significantly?
[06:04] Sofia Alvarez: Model vendor/architecture differences change per-token cost and latency. Our catalog shows relative perf profiles. We can include comparative numbers for the models you care about.
[06:11] Jordan Park: On the logging side, can we push logs to our SIEM? We need to centralize for audits.
[06:15] Marcus Liu: Yes — we have exporters for CloudWatch/Stackdriver and syslog/HTTP webhook sinks for SIEM. We'll include sample configs.
[06:24] [06:35] Keisha Nair: Ok let's recap so nothing falls through: Sofia will share cost export. Marcus will send the test harness and perf baseline. Layla will share endpoints and timelines. Jordan will provide network constraints. We'll schedule the SE deep dive next Tuesday. Anything else?
[06:46] Layla Brooks: One more — can you give an example runbook for fallback if Dedicated capacity is exhausted? We need to document how requests failover to hosted and expected client behavior.
[06:54] Marcus Liu: We'll include a failover runbook: automatic fallback routes, circuit breaker settings, and suggested client-side retries with jitter.
[07:05] [07:15] Amit Desai: Great, and please include the SLA language examples for P95 and availability so procurement can fast-track the review.
[07:22] Sofia Alvarez: We'll include the SLA snippets and procurement checklist.
[07:27] Keisha Nair: Noted. Also, on security evidence — can you include PKI diagrams for the mTLS setup?
[07:32] Marcus Liu: Yep, PKI diagram and example cert rotation process.
[07:38] [07:50] Sofia Alvarez: Alright, call to action — we'll send the packet by Friday and set the SE deep dive for next Tuesday 10am PT. Does that work?
[07:58] Layla Brooks: Works for us.
[08:00] Jordan Park: Works.
[08:02] Keisha Nair: Good. Thanks everyone.
[08:05] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks, we'll follow up with the sheet and the security pack. Bye for now.
[08:08] [08:20] // End of call

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cache" vs "KV cache") and truncated punctuation as captured by the meeting recorder.
